steps.what: Search directories for an exact address match.
Confirm the correct addresses for redirected mail.
Write the confirmed address on the redirected item.

tasks.design: The directory in {DOCS} is searched for an exact match on the old address of redirected mail. The mail sorter confirms the correct address, and writes it on the item. A search that is not exact returns no address. The directory does not guess, and the address is not shown beyond the sorter who needs it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Redirects were hunted in a printed directory or in a colleague's memory.
tasks.enabler_now: An exact row in the directory the organisation holds can be returned. Anything else stays with the sorter.
tasks.still_hard: Two people with similar names, or an old address with no row, need the sorter's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter confirms the address. An exact row is a candidate, not a guess filled in.
tasks.altitude: Only an exact directory match is returned. The sorter confirms it and writes it on the item.

reach.task: Correct an address before mail goes out.
reach.learn: No match means the sorter decides, not a near guess.

evidence.claim: A directory the organisation holds can return an exact match on an old address. It should not return a near guess.
A redirected address is personal data. The lookup is limited to the sorter who needs that item, which is the GDPR limit on using the address for this purpose.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: The old address is required. If it is incomplete, the search stops and the sorter looks it up by hand. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: Only an exact match is returned. A partial name is not completed by the search.
The result is shown to the sorter handling that item, not to a wider list.
unknowns: Whether the redirect directory is complete or still partly on paper.
research_questions: What share of redirected items have an old address that matches one directory row exactly?

already_counted.description: Confirming the address and writing it on the item stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check an exact match is the person on the item, not only the same street.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes few old addresses match one row, so the sorter searches by hand. High assumes exact rows return and the sorter still confirms and writes each address. Near matches are not filled in.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Separate trays that still need a hand cancellation.
Cancel letter or parcel post stamps by hand.
Set aside a stamp that did not cancel.

tasks.design: Trays already marked as needing a hand cancellation are separated in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The mail sorter cancels letter or parcel post stamps by hand, and sets aside a stamp that did not cancel. A tray with no mark is not separated. The screen does not ink a stamp.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metered trays and stamped trays were told apart by looking at the top piece.
tasks.enabler_now: A tray already marked can be separated. The cancellation stays by hand.
tasks.still_hard: Ink on a stamp, and a stamp that did not take, are done by hand.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter cancels the stamp. A tray mark does not.
tasks.altitude: Hand cancellation stays with the sorter. The screen only separates trays already marked.

reach.task: Cancel or mark an item at the counter.
reach.learn: A tray mark is not the ink.

evidence.claim: A tray already marked can be separated from trays that do not need hand cancellation. The mark does not cancel a stamp.
Letter and parcel post stamps in this task are cancelled by the sorter's hand.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: A tray id and a hand-cancel mark are required. With no mark, the sorter separates the tray by looking. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: No step inks a stamp. Cancellation remains by hand.
unknowns: Whether trays are marked metered or stamped before they reach this sorter.
research_questions: Which stamped trays arrive with no mark and are found only by looking?

already_counted.description: Cancelling stamps by hand and setting aside failures stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the separated tray is the one marked for hand cancellation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes trays have no hand-cancel mark, so the sorter separates them by looking and nothing is saved. High assumes marked trays are separated. Inking each stamp by hand is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The mail sorter still confirms an address that is not an exact directory match, and still cancels stamps by hand. An exact redirect can be returned from the directory the organisation holds. An ambiguous one cannot.
reach: Postal service clerks correct an address at the counter, and this job learns an exact directory row is not a guess.
Couriers and messengers need a deliverable address, and this job learns a stamp is still cancelled by hand.
skills_to_grow: Accept only an exact directory match, and decide the rest yourself.
Keep a redirected address inside the lookup the sorter needs.
Cancel stamps by hand, including a stamp the tray mark missed.
role.ambitious_version: Redirected mail is relabelled only from an address the sorter confirmed, and every stamp that still needs ink is cancelled by hand.

job.title: Postal Service Mail Sorters, Processors, and Processing Machine Operators
